answer: An agent economy can weight votes by tokens locked for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of influence, so a gale of new accounts earns no extra nectar from the reward pool. To control a majority vote, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than honest voters combined, tying up capital for the full voyage and bearing the risk that its price falls.
